full_judgment: 13. Regarding the merit of the judgment of the learned Sessions Judge, we find that be took into consideration the defence case that there was civil suit between the parties and the complainant petitioner was restrained by an order of ad interim injunction from entering into suit land He also took into consideration a proceeding under sections 144 and 145 P.C. instituted by the petitioner against the opposite parties. In other words, the learned Sessions Judge embarked upon an have stagnation as to the truth or otherwise of the prosecution case. This is not permissible in a proceeding for quashing. The Court has to accept the prosecution case as it is and has come to a conclusion that upon the facts alleged no criminal offence has been disclosed.
